summary: An Indologist and linguist, Ernest Bender earned his B.A. at Temple University and studied at the University of Pennsylvania under W. Norman Brown, Zellig S. Harris, and Henry M. Hoenigswald. He taught at Penn from 1950 to 1989, becoming professor in 1967.

Working in philosophy, Japanology, and history and archaeology, Ernest Fenollosa graduated from Harvard and studied at the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston. He taught at the University of Tokyo from 1878, was curator at Boston's MFA (1890–1896), and founded Tokyo Fine Arts School.

Ernest John Henry Mackay was a scholar of archaeology and Indology who completed his BA, MA, and DLitt at the University of Bristol. From 1919 to 1922, he served as Custodian of Antiquities for the Government of Mandatory Palestine.

A scholar of religious studies, linguistics, and history, Ernest Renan studied at Saint-Sulpice Seminary and the Collège de France under Eugène Burnouf and Étienne Marc Quatremère. He held posts at the Bibliothèque nationale and served as professor and administrator at the Collège de France.

Ernest Sosa is a philosopher who studied at the University of Miami and the University of Pittsburgh under Roderick M. Chisholm. He served as professor at Brown University starting in 1964 and as Board of Governors Professor at Rutgers University from 1998 to 2006.

Ernst Curtius was an archaeologist and historian who studied at Bonn and Göttingen under Friedrich Gottlieb Welcker and Christian August Brandis. He held professorships at Humboldt University of Berlin and the University of Göttingen (1855–1867), and directed the Altes Museum (~1872–1896).

Ernst Förstemann worked in linguistics and history. He studied at Halle and Berlin under August Friedrich Pott, Karl Lachmann, and Franz Bopp. He served as a librarian at the Fürstlich Stolberg-Stolbergische Bibliothek from 1851 and headed the Dresden library from 1865 to 1887.

Ernst Fürlinger, a scholar of religious studies, Indology, and philosophy, completed his habilitation at the University of Vienna. He was study director at St. Virgil Salzburg (1991–2001), lectured at Vienna (2006–2016), and held research and leadership roles at Krems from 2007.

Art historian Ernst Gombrich earned his PhD at the University of Vienna under Josef Strzygowski. He spent his career primarily at the Warburg Institute as research assistant, fellow, lecturer, reader, and director from 1959 to 1976.

Ernst Haas was an Indologist who studied at Berlin under Albrecht Weber, as well as at Bonn and Tübingen. He joined the British Museum in 1866 and became Professor of Sanskrit at University College London in 1875.

Ernst Haeckel studied at Frederick William University (Humboldt University of Berlin) from around 1854 to 1857. He subsequently held a long-standing academic post at the University of Jena from approximately 1862 to 1909.

Ernst Johann Eitel, a scholar in Sinology and Buddhist studies, earned his MA and PhD at the University of Tübingen. He served with the London Missionary Society (~1865–1879) and taught German language and literature at the University of Adelaide (~1897–1908).

Ernst Kuhn worked in Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies, earning degrees at Tübingen and Halle and studying under Albrecht Weber and Rudolf von Roth. He held professorships at Heidelberg (1875) and Munich (1877–1917).

An Indologist and linguist, Ernst Leumann studied at Zurich, Geneva, Berlin, Leipzig, and Strasbourg under Albrecht Weber. He worked on the Sanskrit-English Dictionary at Oxford, became professor (1884) and rector (1909–1910) at Strasbourg, and later served as honorary professor at Freiburg.

Linguist Ernst Schwarz studied at the German university of Prague from around 1914 to 1920 and completed examinations there in 1921. He later held an academic post at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg from approximately 1953 to 1963.

Ernst Steinkellner, a scholar of Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies, earned his doctorate at Vienna under Erich Frauwallner. He served as professor at Pennsylvania (1971) and directed the Institute for Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia and institutes at Vienna.

Ernst Trumpp was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Tübinger Stift under Rudolf von Roth. After assisting at East India House, he became Privatdozent at Tübingen in 1871 and Professor at the University of Munich from around 1874 to 1885.

Ernst Waldschmidt, a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and Central Asian studies, studied at Kiel and Berlin under Paul Deussen, Emil Sieg, and Heinrich Lüders. He worked at Berlin's Ethnological Museum and held the Indology chair at Göttingen from 1936 to 1965.

Indologist and linguist Ernst Windisch completed his doctorate at Leipzig University, studying under Georg Curtius and Hermann Brockhaus. He held chairs of comparative linguistics at Heidelberg (1872) and Strasbourg (1875), and was a long-serving faculty member at Leipzig.
Ernst Zinn was an academic active in linguistics who held posts at the University of Hamburg (~1947–1954), Saarland University (1951–1956), and the University of Tübingen (~1954–1978).
